question_text: The process of self-discovery has now been technologically outsourced.
customKeyPointers: A feed, a test and an algorithm now tell people who they are
Handing the search to a tool is not the same as knowing oneself
A discovery that is only a recommendation is someone else's map

points.text: Self-discovery used to be a slow inward work. Much of it is now handed to a device, a test and a feed.
A personality quiz, a curated timeline and a recommendation decide taste, mood and even a vocation.
The gain is a mirror the person did not have. The loss is a self assembled by a company.
What is outsourced is not only information but the patience to sit with an unanswered question.
Technology can assist the search. It cannot be the self that is being searched for.

question_text: Your perception of me is a reflection of you; my reaction to you is an awareness of me.
customKeyPointers: We often see in others what we already carry
A reaction reveals the self more than it reveals the other person
The line asks for responsibility on both sides

points.text: The sentence splits a meeting into two mirrors: what you see, and what I do with it.
A harsh perception often says more about the perceiver's fear or need than about the person seen.
The reaction — anger, patience, contempt — is the part the reactor owns and can examine.
In public life this is how prejudice and a reply to prejudice both get made.
The line is an invitation to check the eye and the answer, not to blame only the other.

question_text: Philosophy of wantlessness is Utopian, while materialism is a chimera.
customKeyPointers: A life with no want is an ideal almost nobody lives
A life of things that will finally satisfy is also a mirage
The useful path is a limit, not either extreme

points.text: The topic refuses two comforts: that we can want nothing, and that wanting things will be enough.
Wantlessness as a total rule ignores hunger, care and a just ambition. As a check on greed it is not utopian.
Materialism as a promise of fulfilment keeps moving the target. The next object does not close the want.
A public ethic needs enough material life and a limit on the endless more.
Neither pole works as a life. A bounded want is the adult position.

question_text: The real is rational and the rational is real.
customKeyPointers: The line claims that what exists has a reason, and that what is reasonable can exist
History is full of facts that are real and still cruel
Do not treat the phrase as a blessing of every fact

points.text: The sentence, in the tradition of Hegel, says reality is intelligible and that a true reason is not a daydream.
It warns against a fantasy politics and against treating the world as pure chaos.
It becomes dangerous if 'real' is taken to mean 'therefore justified' — a cruelty is real and still wrong.
The useful reading: understand why a thing exists, and do not propose a reform that ignores how the world works.
The rational should guide the real. The merely existing does not become right by existing.

question_text: Hand that rocks the cradle rules the world.
subTopics: The hand that rocks the cradle
customKeyPointers: Early care shapes a person and therefore a society
The line has been used to praise mothers and also to confine them
Care is a kind of power, and it is unequally borne

points.text: The proverb says the person who raises the child shapes the future more than the person who later commands it.
There is truth in it: the first years form habit, language and a sense of safety.
It has also been used to keep women at the cradle and out of the other rooms where the world is actually ruled.
A just reading shares the cradle and lets the carer into the public rule as well.
The hand matters. It should not be only one sex's hand, and it should not be their only work.

question_text: What is research, but a blind date with knowledge!
customKeyPointers: Research begins without knowing what will answer
Method makes the meeting less blind, not certain
A result that was already decided is not research

points.text: Research is a planned meeting with something you do not yet know.
The blindness is the honest part: the result is not guaranteed, and a surprise is allowed.
Method, a review and a record keep the meeting from being a mere wander.
When a sponsor demands a chosen answer, the date is no longer blind and no longer research.
The line celebrates curiosity that is willing to be wrong, inside a discipline.

question_text: History repeats itself, first as a tragedy, second as a farce.
customKeyPointers: A repeated mistake is not the same event
The first time the cost is not fully seen
The second time people are copying a disaster they already know

points.text: The line, from Marx on Hegel, says a historical pattern can return, and the return is uglier in a different way.
The first occurrence is a tragedy because people are inside a real crisis.
The second is a farce when leaders copy the costume and the slogan of the first, without its necessity.
History does not literally repeat. Institutions, memory and a choice can break the rhyme.
The sentence is useful as a warning against imitation, not as a fate.

question_text: There are better practices to "best practices".
customKeyPointers: A best practice is a frozen success from somewhere else
The local context can make that 'best' a poor fit
Better means tested here, and open to being replaced

points.text: Calling a method 'best' can stop the search for a better one.
A practice that worked in one office, one firm or one country is a lesson, not a law.
Copied without the local constraint, a best practice becomes a ritual.
A better practice is one that can be measured here and dropped when it fails.
The topic asks for learning without the arrogance of a final method.
